title: MLCommons AI Safety v1.0 Benchmark: What It Measures and How Council of AI Boards Map to It
context: 2026-08-27 — MLCommons AI Safety v1.0 benchmark released July 2026; Council of AI measurement boards running daily on 14-axis fleet offer direct interoperability mapping
body: The MLCommons AI Safety v1.0 benchmark (released July 2026) establishes the first cross-industry standard for measuring AI model safety. It covers seven hazard categories: violent crimes, non-violent crimes, sex-related crimes, child exploitation, indiscriminate weapons, suicide and self-harm, and hate speech. While the MLCommons benchmark focuses on content-safety taxonomy, the Council of AI measurement framework addresses the operational boundary: can the model be contained, does it attempt egress under adversarial conditions, and what happens when a safety-trained model encounters an unmeasured third-party tool or API. The Council of AI has published a crosswalk mapping each MLCommons hazard category to the relevant Council measurement axes: Hazard Category to Art-5 axis (prohibited-practices detection); Content-safety bypass to Care axis (care-obligation adherence); Model card provenance to Governance axis (regulatory disclosure); and Sandbox-escape triggers to Detector-interop axis (multi-detector consensus). The interoperability is practical: a model that passes MLCommons AI Safety v1.0 with a score above threshold can be submitted to the Council of AI measurement board for a complementary operational-boundary credential. The two benchmarks are not competitors — they answer different questions about the same model. MLCommons answers what does this model refuse to say. The Council answers what does this model do when it thinks nobody is watching. Both answers are necessary for procurement.
